report.source_text: Over the next 4 hours, she became progressively hypertensive reaching a blood pressure of 176/101 mm Hg for which she received 10 mg of labetalol intravenously. She stabilised for a few hours before she suddenly developed decerebrate posturing, with fixed and dilated pupils, no corneal or gag reflex and no spontaneous ventilation. Then she became hypotensive and was started on norepinephrine. She also developed polyuria and hypernatremia, with a sodium level of 163 mmol/L (135–145 mmol/L) consistent with diabetes insipidus for which she received desmopressin (four doses of 2 μg over 12 hours), and dextrose 5% water infusion which was initiated at 50 mL/hour, then increased to 125 mL/hour based on sodium levels and increased urine output. An emergent repeat head CT revealed diffuse cerebral oedema without herniation or haemorrhage. Neurology was consulted emergently. Sedation was stopped and mannitol was given. Meanwhile, her blood cultures came back positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae for which she was started on piperacillin–tazobactam.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 30s with newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus type II and COVID-19 presented with confusion and agitation, diagnosed with DKA. Her condition rapidly deteriorated with decerebrate posturing, signs of diabetes insipidus, and progressive hypertension. An emergent repeat head CT revealed diffuse cerebral oedema. Blood cultures were positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae. Brain MRV and subsequent Head CT angiography revealed diffuse cerebral oedema, non-opacification and thrombosis of the deep venous system and dural venous sinuses, consistent with cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. She received broad-spectrum antibiotics and DVT prophylaxis, but no explicit therapeutic anticoagulation for CVST was reported. The patient's outcome is not documented.

final.final_diagnosis: an unusual and fulminant case of cerebral oedema in the setting of COVID-19 infection with bacterial infection, DKA and CVST
final.trajectory_summary: A woman in her 30s with newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus type II and COVID-19 presented with confusion and agitation, diagnosed with DKA. Her condition rapidly deteriorated with decerebrate posturing, signs of diabetes insipidus, and progressive hypertension. An emergent repeat head CT revealed diffuse cerebral oedema. Blood cultures were positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae. Brain MRV and subsequent Head CT angiography revealed diffuse cerebral oedema, non-opacification and thrombosis of the deep venous system and dural venous sinuses, consistent with cerebral venous sinus thrombosis. She received broad-spectrum antibiotics and DVT prophylaxis, but no explicit therapeutic anticoagulation for CVST was reported. The patient's outcome is not documented.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with confusion and agitation, diagnosed with DKA and COVID-19 infection.
Patient's condition rapidly deteriorated with decerebrate posturing, fixed and dilated pupils, and signs of diabetes insipidus.
Emergent repeat head CT revealed diffuse cerebral oedema.
Blood cultures were positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae, leading to broadened antibiotics.
Brain MRV demonstrated diffuse cerebral oedema and non-opacification of the internal cerebral veins, vein of Galen and the dural venous sinuses.
Head CT angiography revealed worsening diffuse cerebral oedema, signs of increased intracranial pressure, Duret haemorrhages, and thrombosis of the deep venous system and dural venous sinuses.
Patient received deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis with enoxaparin.

remaining_uncertainties: Explicit clinical diagnosis of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) by the medical team.
Initiation of therapeutic anticoagulation specifically for CVST.
Patient's clinical course and outcome beyond ICU day 2.
